clue.text: Money-changing villain suffering current depreciation?

definitions.note: agio is the charge made for changing money; the clue's adjective names the trade

indicators.note: suffering says the villain's name undergoes the change described next
a depreciation is a fall in value, so in this down light the current letter slides lower

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A crooked money-changer finds his money is losing value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depreciation' is a pun: the I drops two places down the villain's name, which in a down entry means lower in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is the premium or percentage charged when exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: Metalworker is in time to work with this medium

indicators.note: set to work, these letters are made to operate in a fresh order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An artist who handles metal is in time to start on a new medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is a craftsman who makes and mends articles of tin or tinplate.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well asked for disused goods?

parts.note: bade is an old-fashioned past tense of bid, meaning asked for; 'disused' flags the archaism
G is the abbreviation for good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: A rogue requested goods that nobody uses any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disused' looks like it describes the goods, but it marks the word for 'asked for' as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a scoundrel or worthless person.

clue.text: Cross palm with investment of a sub-£1,000 postal order

indicators.note: a palm invested with these letters has them wrapped inside it

parts.note: the coco is the coconut palm

indicators.note: sub means under, so in this down light the A goes below the thousand letter

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in £1K
PO is the abbreviation for postal order

explanation.surface: Someone bribes a palm-reader by slipping in a small postal order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross palm' suggests bribery or fortune-telling, but 'Cross' is the definition and the palm is the coconut tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockapoo is a dog crossbred from a cocker spaniel and a poodle.

clue.text: Nitrogen cycle of 26 chemist

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

indicators.note: cycling the letters of that answer moves its opening pair round to the end

parts.note: the answer to 26 Across

explanation.surface: A chemist is linked to the nitrogen cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Walther Nernst was a German physical chemist and Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nernst won the 1920 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work in thermochemistry.

clue.text: Order two of each in the end, clever clogs?

indicators.note: to order the words is to put their letters into a new sequence
in the end points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A know-it-all orders two of everything in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' is a British phrase for a show-off; here 'clever' gives only its last letter and 'clogs' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clogs are wooden shoes, an example of things worn on the feet, hence the question mark.

clue.text: "A little cryptic", our setters' line

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Crossword setters declare that their policy is to be only slightly cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of action, as in a course of action, is a direction or route taken.

clue.text: A way to escape the Yard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Chambers gives ... as a gap through a hedge by which a hare or other animal escapes
second meaning: a yard or street of stables, now often converted to houses

explanation.surface: A criminal finds a route to slip away from Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, but it is a stable yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A mews is a row of stables round a courtyard; the escape sense is a rare dictionary meaning.

clue.text: Fly solo over diminishing country steeped in history

indicators.note: the over and shortened country are soaked inside the word for history

parts.note: someone who is history is gone
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: diminishing cuts the country's name short by its final letter

parts.note: Italy is the country

explanation.surface: A pilot flies alone over a shrinking land with a long past.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly solo is an idiom for acting independently, without help from anyone else.

clue.text: Reviving air mail area code for the Emerald City?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fresh bracing air, popularly said to be found at the seaside

definitions.text: mail area code for the Emerald City?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split 2,3 it reads like a postcode, OZ plus a district number, for the capital of the Land of Oz

explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz in The Wizard of Oz; a British postcode district is letters plus a number, as in SW1.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is loosely used for the invigorating fresh air of the coast.

clue.text: Mick, call Ms Hillary? Friends again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: said out loud these words are Michaelmas and Hilary, the Oxford University autumn and spring terms, so they are terms as heard in speech
second meaning: friendly enough to talk to each other again after a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas and Hilary are the names of Oxford's autumn and spring terms; the clue spells them as they sound, giving the phrase a literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on speaking terms is an idiom for being friendly enough to talk again after a quarrel.

clue.text: Prize-fighters as title contenders will punch but finish last

indicators.note: the fighters' letters punch into the word for but, ending up inside it

parts.note: bar means except, as but does
the ring is boxing, or the boxers collectively
contenders for a title are up there with the best

explanation.surface: Boxers contending for a title will throw punches but end up losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear is an idiom for coming last in a procession or race.

clue.text: In proposal, one's managed to make mark

indicators.note: in the proposal word, the one is now 'managed', so that letter is swapped out

parts.note: a bid is an offer or proposal
I is the Roman numeral one; one's is 'one is'
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: In a proposal, one person has succeeded in making an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is an identifying mark, such as one burned onto livestock.

clue.text: See 12
Official subject line, Adam emailing back the Almighty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a local official in medieval England

definitions.text: subject line, Adam emailing back the Almighty?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split 2,3, an email reply from Adam to God about his wife would be headed '...'

explanation.walkthrough: RE is the usual subject-line tag on an email reply; Eve is Adam's wife in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a chief magistrate or steward of a town or district in Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: Sequence in which five notes becomes four imbues new Michael Tippett work

indicators.note: the altered scale soaks into the rearranged name, sitting inside it
new shows the name's letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the name Michael gives its seven letters as fodder

indicators.note: becomes signals that the five notes are replaced by the word four

parts.note: the sol-fa scale do re mi fa so la ti
the five middle notes of the scale, re to la
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical description of a Michael Tippett piece in which a note sequence is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol-fa is the do-re-mi system of naming scale notes; 'five notes becomes four' means the word four takes the place of the middle five, and the result sits inside the jumbled name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Child of Our Time is Michael Tippett's oratorio, first performed in 1944.

clue.text: Romantic musical all about Sandi T's right-hand man?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of all are turned around into a different order

parts.note: Sandi Toksvig hosts the TV panel show QI; Alan Davies sits on her right, and 'Sandi T' style he is Alan D

explanation.surface: A romantic musical concerns the sidekick of a TV host.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a long-running British comedy quiz show; Alan Davies is its permanent panellist beside the host.
explanation.definitionFit: La La Land is the 2016 Hollywood film musical about a love affair between a jazz pianist and an actress.

clue.text: Ordinary singer and ordinary song work together!

parts.note: a rat, an informer, sings to the police
O for ordinary again
Rio is a 1982 hit song by Duran Duran

explanation.surface: An everyday singer and an everyday song combine in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks musical, but it is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical composition for voices and orchestra on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Puritan resistance quelled by one in fair position

indicators.note: the resistance letter is held down and contained by the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
onside, in sport, means legitimately placed
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Puritan's resistance is put down by one who is well placed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironsides were Oliver Cromwell's Puritan cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironside was one of Cromwell's soldiers, typically a devout Puritan.

clue.text: Old two-piece settee grandly unveiled repeatedly then chosen for similar

parts.note: settee with its outer letters stripped twice leaves TT, which reads as 'double T'

indicators.note: unveiled repeatedly means the covering outer letters come off, and then the next outer pair as well

parts.note: taken as written, then stripped twice

indicators.note: for similar treatment, chosen is unveiled too, just once

parts.note: taken as written, then stripped once

explanation.surface: An antique two-seater sofa is grandly revealed and then picked for a matching one.
explanation.walkthrough: Doublet and hose was the jacket and leggings of Tudor men. 'Two-piece' suggests furniture, which the settee supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet and hose was the traditional two-part outfit worn by men in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: To avoid embarrassment, trouser-wearer braces himself for this maintenance bill!

definitions.text: To avoid embarrassment, trouser-wearer braces himself for this maintenance bill!

parts.words: To avoid embarrassment, trouser-wearer braces himself for this maintenance bill!
parts.note: braces hold trousers in place so they stay where they belong; the phrase for that is also a word for the cost of maintenance

explanation.surface: A man wearing trousers prepares himself for an embarrassing repair bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braces himself' looks like steeling oneself, but braces are the British word for trouser suspenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost of keeping something in good condition, a maintenance expense.

clue.text: Sustained work done by fielding side, having dropped opposition's opener

indicators.note: the opening letter of opposition drops lower, which in this down light moves it to the end

parts.note: in cricket the fielding side's job is to get ten batsmen out
first letter of opposition

explanation.surface: A cricket team in the field puts in sustained work but drops an opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' suggests a dropped catch; it moves the letter down. A side is all out once ten wickets fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuto is a musical direction meaning a note should be held for its full length.

clue.text: See 19
Like protagonists in Holy Grail, we assume with a new soundtrack

definitions.text: Like protagonists in Holy Grail, we assume
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the knights of the Grail legend were made knights with a sword tap
second meaning: a film given replacement dialogue, often in another language

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Monty Python and the Holy Grail, a film whose characters are knights.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub is both to confer knighthood and to replace a film's soundtrack with another.

clue.text: Position: kilometre between; hence zero — then eventually in boundless supply!

definitions.text: Position: kilometre between; hence zero — then eventually in boundless supply!

indicators.note: between puts the kilometre letter inside the word for position

parts.note: lie means position, as in the lie of the land
K is short for kilometre

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero

indicators.note: eventually picks out the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A wry description of waiting for a bus: none for ages, then an endless supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that London buses never come, then several come together; the clue's second half describes this as well as giving the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things that are absent for a long wait and then arrive all at once.

clue.text: Fail to keep to having a shave

indicators.note: a shave trims away the edges, so the word is cut back at its first and final letters

parts.note: a door pulled to is closed

explanation.surface: Someone forgets a promise to shave.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose something is to fail to retain it, as when a team fails to keep a lead.

clue.text: "Class" or "type" nails it

indicators.note: nails it means the words grip the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Calling something a class or a type gets it exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind, class or category of things.

clue.text: Doctor Zhivago author held this back

indicators.note: held means the answer is only the part gripped in the middle of the author's surname, its outer letters falling away

parts.note: Boris Pasternak wrote Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: The author of Doctor Zhivago held back this book.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside PASTERNAK, so the two letters at each end go. 'Held this back' reads as withholding, but 'back' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear or back part of a ship.

clue.text: Warm and affectionate nurses upset Charlie?

indicators.note: nurses means holds, as a nurse holds a baby, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: tender means warm and affectionate
to ail is to trouble or upset

explanation.surface: A warm, kind nurse is looking after a troubled patient named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: A charlie is British slang for a fool; a tail-ender is a cricket batsman low in the order and usually poor at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is a weak late-order batsman, so the question mark marks the hapless charlie as an example.
